ARTHUR: You cannot just ignore the data and hope the problem resolves itself.
BEATRICE: I am not ignoring it, Arthur, I am simply interpreting it differently than you are.
ARTHUR: There is no other way to interpret a deficit of this magnitude.
BEATRICE: We have faced worse quarters and managed to pull through without panicking.
ARTHUR: Panic is what I would call sitting quietly while the ship takes on water.
BEATRICE: And I would call your approach frantically drilling holes in the hull to let the water out.
ARTHUR: That does not even make sense.
BEATRICE: It makes perfect sense if you think about your reactionary measures.
ARTHUR: My measures are based on hard numbers and cold reality.
BEATRICE: Your reality leaves no room for human capital or long-term growth.
ARTHUR: Long-term growth will not matter if we go bankrupt by the end of next month.
BEATRICE: We are not going bankrupt.
ARTHUR: You keep saying that like it is a magical spell that will balance the ledger.
BEATRICE: And you keep shouting doom like it will somehow generate revenue.
ARTHUR: I am just being realistic.
BEATRICE: No, Arthur, you are being terrified, and there is a distinct difference.
ARTHUR: Fine. If you have a better plan that does not involve freezing budgets, I am all ears.
BEATRICE: My plan involves restructuring our debt and investing in the new marketing campaign.
ARTHUR: Spending more money to fix a lack of money. Brilliant.
BEATRICE: You have to spend money to make money, Arthur. It is the oldest rule in business.
ARTHUR: It is also the quickest way to liquidation if the gamble fails.
BEATRICE: Life is a gamble, especially this line of work.
ARTHUR: I prefer calculated risks to blind faith.
BEATRICE: Then trust my calculations for once instead of hiding behind your spreadsheets.
ARTHUR: Those spreadsheets are the only reason we still have offices to sit in.
BEATRICE: And my vision is the only reason those offices have any future.
ARTHUR: We are going in circles.
BEATRICE: We always go in circles when you refuse to see the bigger picture.
ARTHUR: The picture looks pretty small when the frame is collapsing.
BEATRICE: Then let me help you hold the frame together.
ARTHUR: By doing it your way?
BEATRICE: By finding a compromise somewhere in the middle.
ARTHUR: The middle usually means nobody gets what they want.
BEATRICE: Or it means both of us get a version of what we need.
ARTHUR: Let hear your compromise, then.
BEATRICE: We freeze half the departmental budgets and fund the marketing pilot.
ARTHUR: Only a pilot?
BEATRICE: A pilot. If it fails by month two, we pull the plug and do it your way.
ARTHUR: And if it succeeds?
BEATRICE: Then we fund the rest of the campaign and you buy me lunch.
ARTHUR: It is a deal, but do not expect an expensive restaurant if the pilot tanks.
